equity_bridge.item: Pending Roku acquisition: 85% close probability x c.-$3.5bn IV-basis dilution
equity_bridge.note: Consideration for c.153m Roku diluted shares = $14.7bn cash + c.148m FOXA shares. Roku standalone on a house owner-FCF basis (CY2025 OCF $484m less SBC $354m less capex $5m = $125m; H1 CY2026 $323m; c.$0.5bn CY2026E growing 15%) is worth c.$16bn equity incl. its $2.0bn cash, plus c.$3bn for $400m run-rate cost synergies net of integration cost = c.$19bn of value acquired. On an IV basis the deal moves base-case value from E/427.6m to (E + 19,000 - 14,700)/575.9m, c.-$8/share or c.-$3.5bn at a $60 standalone IV (-$5bn at the $63 FOXA market price). Close probability 85%: both controlling holders have signed support agreements and ROKU trades within c.3% of implied consideration; residual risk is antitrust/foreign approval. The FanDuel 18.6% call option (strike c.$4.7bn escalating 5%/yr, expires Dec 2030) is NOT valued: exercising needs c.$5bn of cash Fox will not have post-Roku; it is unquantified upside noted in the bull narrative.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: 10-year base-case revenue CAGR (FY2026 -> FY2036) after netting the World Cup / Super Bowl / election cycle; equity CAGR is suppressed by c.$7bn of buybacks and revenue CAGR is inflated by Tubi scaling from near zero and an FY2026 World Cup year
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 1.1% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 5.8% and EPS 3yr CAGR 18.7%: divergence >30%. Book value is held down by $7.0bn of repurchases FY2022-FY2026; EPS is distorted by the FY2023 Dominion settlement ($787.5m) base and FY2025/26 fair-value swings on the Flutter stake. Neither series is a clean growth anchor, hence the mid-cycle judgment above.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net debt throughout). Owner-FCF series FY2021 2,008 / FY2023 1,369 / FY2026 1,336 (reported 2,155 / 1,443 / 1,468). Owner-FCF CAGRs sit c.0.4-1.4pp below reported because SBC has grown from $147m to $132m on a smaller share base (0.77% of revenue); SBC is immaterial to the valuation here. FCF history is event-driven: FY2025 $2,993m (Super Bowl LIX + election + $0.6bn WC inflow) vs FY2026 $1,468m (World Cup rights paid, FOX One launch, -$1.4bn WC); the 3-year average unlevered owner FCF of c.$2.2bn (13.8% of revenue) is the mid-cycle anchor the year-1 projection is checked against.

scenario_narratives.base: Franchise holds; Tubi/FOX One offset linear decline; NFL renewal costs c.2.5pp of margin from FY2031; Roku closes and is mildly IV-dilutive. Revenue c.+1.3%/yr through the event cycle, adjusted EBITDA margin drifting from 22.5% to 20%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Digital (Tubi, FOX One, Roku data) outgrows linear erosion, NFL renewal absorbed, adjusted margin c.23% held, FanDuel option monetised (unmodelled), Roku synergies make the deal neutral.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sports-driven cord-cutting accelerates, NFL renewal at +50% from FY2031, Tubi decelerates, Roku integration and leverage strain; revenue -1.3%/yr and adjusted margin to c.16%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fox is valued as a mature, ad-cyclical US media franchise on a strict owner-FCF basis: Adjusted EBITDA is haircut 2pp to a cash basis for the structural sports-rights working-capital drag, SBC is expensed, cash tax ramps from the Disney step-up shelter to the 24% GAAP rate, and the terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (in line with today's c.12x EV/mid-cycle FCF, so no re-rating is assumed). The revenue path is deliberately cyclic (elections, Super Bowl rotation, World Cup) rather than smoothed. The pending Roku acquisition is treated as a live corporate action: FOX standalone is valued and the deal enters as a single probability-weighted bridge line at its expected IV-basis dilution, with the scenario narratives carrying the range.
key_risks_to_valuation: Roku acquisition: if it closes, share count rises c.35% (to c.576m) and net debt by c.$12-13bn; the -$3.0bn bridge line is a point estimate on a deal whose day-one market reaction was -27% (FOX $61 -> $45, June 2026); a rebuild post-close must re-anchor shares and net debt to the combined entity
NFL renewal after the 2029-30 season: every 10% rise in the c.$2.2bn annual fee is c.1.3pp of margin; the base case carries c.2.5pp from FY2031, the bear 6pp
Working-capital treatment: the 2pp cash-EBITDA haircut is a judgment on a series that swung +$0.6bn/-$1.4bn in the last two years; each 1pp is c.$4/share
Cash tax: the $2.4bn deferred tax asset is assumed to be consumed by FY2035; a faster consumption or legislative change moves value c.$2-3/share
Terminal multiple: 12x owner FCF is the binding constraint in base and bull; Gordon at 8.5%/1.5% would be 14.5x
Class B (FOX) trades c.10% below Class A (FOXA); the IV is class-agnostic, so the discount is either a mispricing or a governance/liquidity charge the model does not make

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation add-back $132m (XBRL). No combined equity-award figure is published and net-share-settlement withholding is not separately tagged, so the add-back is used as-is; the true cost is modestly higher.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z Nasdaq regular close (Friday), FOX Class B voting shares; FOXA Class A closed at a c.10% premium the same day
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-08-04 (10-K cover: 199.40m Class A + 220.25m Class B = 419.65m) plus 8.0m dilutive awards (Q3 FY2026 diluted 432m less basic 424m)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks ($2.0bn in FY2026 incl. a $1.5bn ASR, $1.0bn in each of FY2022-FY2025) fund the flat count. The pending Roku merger would issue c.148m Class A shares; that is non-SBC issuance and is carried in the equity bridge, not the count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10y UST c.4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta c.0.85 = cost of equity c.8.5%; pre-tax debt cost c.4.7% (3.7% after tax) on $6.6bn of senior notes against a c.$24bn market cap gives a capital-weighted 7.4%. Rounded up to 8.5% for a mature ad-cyclical media company with structural linear decline and a pending leveraged acquisition (pro-forma net leverage c.2.8x). Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, the NFL renewal and the Roku outcome are charged in the flows and the probability weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: single lease cost sits inside operating expenses, i.e. inside Adjusted EBITDA, so no separate lease charge; $962m operating lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI share of net income $42m in FY2026, c.2.5%); the NCI stock ($100m equity NCI + $86m redeemable NCI at 30 Jun 2026) is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Fox is a US operating media company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; not a REIT/bank/holdco. LIVE CORPORATE ACTION: Fox is the ACQUIRER in the pending Roku merger (signed 14 Jun 2026, $96 cash + 0.9693 FOXA per Roku share, c.$22bn EV, expected close H1 CY2027, LGC Holdco and Anthony Wood support agreements signed). All reported figures are FOX standalone, so the DCF values FOX standalone and carries the deal as a probability-weighted equity-bridge line (see equity_bridge); the three scenarios carry the operating axes. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: the ebitda_margin_path is a CASH-EBITDA basis = Adjusted EBITDA margin (FY2026 22.8% = $3,906m / $17,126m; FY2025 22.2%; FY2024 c.20.6%) LESS 2.0pp for the structural working-capital outflow from sports-rights cash payments running ahead of amortisation (FY2024-FY2026 average operating working-capital outflow c.$300-400m/yr; FY2026 alone c.-$1.4bn on World Cup/FOX One timing, FY2025 +$0.6bn). Modelling it as a margin haircut rather than wc_capture keeps the drag in place in the bear case, where revenue falls but contracted rights escalators do not; wc_capture_pct is therefore 0. CASH TAX: the Disney-transaction basis step-up ($2.4bn deferred tax asset) keeps cash tax well below the 24% GAAP rate (FY2024 c.11%, FY2025 16.8%, FY2026 14.7%); the path ramps 16% -> 24% over the decade so the shelter is consumed, not perpetuated. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped ($127m FY2026) because the company is net DEBT (+$2.4bn), and the component build is unlevered anyway; last_fcf is reported FCF less SBC only and is an anchor, not a projection base. REVENUE PATH is deliberately cyclic: political advertising (even calendar years -> odd fiscal years), Super Bowl rotation (Fox: Feb 2025 = FY2025, Feb 2029 = FY2029, Feb 2033 = FY2033), and the 2026 World Cup (June group stage in FY2026, July knockouts in FY2027). NFL: current contract runs through the 2029-30 season (FY2030); management declined early renegotiation (Aug 2026); the base case takes c.2.5pp of adjusted margin from FY2031 for a rights step-up, the bear c.6pp. Class B (FOX) trades c.10% below Class A (FOXA); per-share IV is class-agnostic and is compared with the FOX quote.

bear.narrative: Cord-cutting accelerates to high-single digits as sports move to streaming bundles and rate rises stop covering volume; FOX One cannibalises rather than adds; Tubi growth slows to the teens as YouTube and Amazon take CTV ad share; the NFL renewal from FY2031 lands at the +50% the league is seeking (c.6pp of margin) because Fox cannot afford to lose the NFC package; a Fox News legal/advertiser episode recurs. Revenue shrinks c.1.3%/yr and adjusted margin falls to c.16%. Roku integration disappoints and the combined company's leverage forces a buyback pause.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +1.5%: midterm political (Nov 2026) and the July 2026 World Cup knockout rounds plus Tubi (+25-35%) and distribution rate rises, against the loss of the June 2026 group stage and linear ad erosion. FY2028 trough (no event), FY2029 Super Bowl LXIII + presidential election, FY2030 trough, FY2033 Super Bowl LXVII + presidential. Nets to c.1.3%/yr: distribution flat-to-up (subs -6-8%/yr vs rates +7-10%), linear ads -3-5%/yr, Tubi/FOX One adding c.$250-350m/yr.
base.margin_rationale: Cash-EBITDA basis (Adjusted EBITDA margin less 2.0pp working-capital drag, see inputs.notes). Adjusted margin held c.22.5% through FY2029 (FOX One losses narrowing offset cord-cutting), stepping to c.20% from FY2031 for the NFL renewal (contract expires after the 2029-30 season; current fee c.$2.2bn/yr, league seeking +50%; partial offset from NFL ad-rate growth).
base.narrative: Fox holds its franchise: Fox News keeps c.60% cable-news share, the NFL/MLB/Big Ten/NASCAR slate keeps the broadcast network must-carry, Tubi compounds to a $2.5bn+ profitable AVOD business and FOX One reaches breakeven, together roughly offsetting mid-single-digit linear subscriber decline. The NFL renewal from FY2031 costs c.2.5pp of margin. The Roku deal closes (85%) and is mildly value-dilutive on an IV basis but strategically neutral.

bull.narrative: Tubi sustains 25%+ growth to a $3-4bn business and becomes a material EBITDA contributor; FOX One scales as the bundle for cord-nevers and lifts distribution revenue above the linear decline; digital advertising (Tubi + Roku data) more than replaces linear ad erosion; the NFL renewal is absorbed with a c.1pp margin cost because NFL ad pricing keeps rising and the package expands. Adjusted margin holds c.23%. The FanDuel option (18.6% at c.$4.7bn strike, Dec 2030) is monetised or exercised, worth an unmodelled $1-2bn. Roku synergies exceed the $400m run-rate and the deal becomes IV-neutral.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the pending $22bn cash-and-stock Roku acquisition takes pro-forma leverage to c.2.8x, the NFL renewal is a known large cost step-up the company has chosen to defer rather than resolve, and the distribution base (47% of revenue) is in structural unit decline. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs Tubi, FOX One, Roku synergies and a benign NFL renewal to all go right. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
